purpose: Taliglucerase alfa is used to treat a rare inherited condition called Gaucher disease. In Gaucher disease, your body does not have enough of a certain enzyme, which causes fatty substances to build up in your organs and bones. This medicine helps reduce symptoms like an enlarged spleen or liver, anemia, and bone problems.
how_it_works: Your body normally makes an enzyme called glucocerebrosidase that breaks down a fatty substance called glucocerebroside. In Gaucher disease, this enzyme does not work properly, causing the fat to build up in your cells. Taliglucerase alfa is a man-made version of this enzyme that replaces what your body is missing, helping to clear out the fatty buildup.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include joint pain, headache, dizziness, nausea, stomach pain, back pain, and tiredness. Some people may have a reaction during or shortly after the infusion, such as flushing, itching, or changes in heart rate or blood pressure. These reactions are usually managed by slowing the infusion or giving other medicines beforehand.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you have signs of a serious allergic reaction such as difficulty breathing, chest tightness, severe rash, or swelling of the face and throat. Some patients develop antibodies to this medicine, which may reduce how well it works over time. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using this medication.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion directly into a vein, usually every two weeks. The dose is based on your body weight, and each infusion typically takes about 60 to 120 minutes. Your healthcare team will monitor you during and after each infusion.
